searchText: I love how participation on mainnet is much better than on pyrmont which is still largely controlled by core dev validators. Mainnet participation is still rising with new validators coming in. I imagine this is in everybody’s minds but has anyone learned anything more about how the slashing occurred And why aren’t both blocks shown? the relevant data/signatures are here https://beaconcha.in/block/6669#proposer-slashings > And why aren’t both blocks shown? in the block explorer?? most nodes likely won't include a conflicting block in their tree when more than one slasher is present, which one gets to appear under "slashed by"? who gets the reward? Another question: does finality on ETH2 apply to anything on ETH1 network? "slashed by" refers to the first block proposer that included the slashing. I see, the one who gets the lion's share of reward. thanks. Another question: does finality on ETH2 apply to anything on ETH1 network? In any way on how business is done on Ethereum? yes I want to know that too i asked around on Prysm and they seem to think it's likely two validator processes with the same keys yeah, seems very likely they produced two blocks with different bodies so likely on a different node with a slightly different attestation pool but that would also require being pointed to two different beacon nodes no? ie saparate locations that viewed the tree differently? I presume a slight timing difference when requested from a BN could result ina different block too yep likely two separate instances the blocks have the same parent so tehy saw the block tree the same but they have different contents so their operation pool was slightly different it seems more likely the items in the block body when requesting from the beacon were different, probably attestations yeah i wish there was more introspection available into such occurances, given that right now its more likely to be operator error, than malicious/nefarious activity meant to harm the chain but i understand also that intent is indistinguishable <@!311971895828283393> i apologize for asking the same thing i asked you on Prysm, here as well, but how does it work when attesters to the block that's slashed get panalized too? or have I invented that concept in my mind entirely and thats not part of the spec i thought there was something about the offender + the attesters on that head as well, something about the 1/3 vs the 2/3 majority, finding out the 1/3 wasn't being 'honest validators' weren't being* It wouldn't be at all fair to punish attesters. For example a bad proposer could send one block to half the network, and a different block to the other half - neither side would know they were doing something wrong. The attesters to the block that got included will receive rewards as usual. Attesters to the other block will miss out on the correct head reward. im sorry, i didn't mean that this should be the case, i was asking if i misunderstood what i read before? is this not what happens in the spec right now at all, nobody punished other than the offending proposer/attester getting slashed Yes, exactly. And I didn't read it as a suggestion 🙂 just explaining why we don't do it. i see 🙂 thank you for the explanation and response! A short update re the slashing incident earlier today: I have just talked to the slashed validator and we found the issue at hand. They had another nimbus instance running with the same keys. Good to know (bad for the user, obviously, but that's a far better result than a potential client issue). (post merge) would gas be cheap enough that any instance at start up could call a smart contract with a validator key + host-specific magic number, that would allow validators running with the same key on a different host to see that call had been made by the key and take some action before a slashing condition?
